title: ETGS: Explicit Thermodynamics Gaussian Splatting for Dynamic Thermal Reconstruction
abstract: We propose ETGS, a method for reconstructing dynamic thermal scenes by embedding explicit thermodynamic modeling into 3D Gaussian Splatting. Each Gaussian is equipped with physically interpretable thermal parameters, and its thermaldynamics evolution is described by a first-order heat-transfer ODE with an analytical closed-form solution. This formulation avoids numerical integration, enables efficient rendering at arbitrary timestamps, and naturally handles irregular sampling and out-of-order observations. We also introduce the Rapid Heat Dynamics (RHD) dataset, which provides millisecond-aligned RGB–IR image pairs covering typical thermal processes such as cooling, warming, heating, and heat transfer. Experiments on RHD show that ETGS captures rapid thermal dynamics more accurately than existing static and dynamic baselines, while maintaining training and rendering efficiency close to that of static 3DGS. Code and dataset will be released.
problem: Reconstructing dynamic thermal scenes requires handling temporal evolution and irregular sampling in thermal imaging.
approach: Embeds explicit thermodynamic modeling into 3D Gaussian Splatting with heat-transfer ODEs and analytical solutions for efficient rendering.
contribution: Captures rapid thermal dynamics more accurately than static and dynamic baselines while maintaining efficiency comparable to static 3DGS.
